routing_policy: Primary category names the barrier to repair. Secondary categories name other relevant specialists, not additional failures. categories.title: Content alternatives and timed media
categories.signal_terms: Images, icons, charts, CAPTCHA, transcripts, captions, descriptions, sign language, live media
categories.diagnostic_question: Is information unavailable without seeing or hearing a particular media modality?
categories.common_misclassification: Avoid generic alt text and confusing synchronized media with audio-only content.

categories.title: Structure and reading order
categories.signal_terms: Heading hierarchy, lists, tables, linear order, landmarks and semantic identification
categories.diagnostic_question: Does presentation imply a relationship or sequence that is unavailable programmatically?
categories.common_misclassification: A visual screenshot cannot confirm the accessibility tree or DOM reading order.

categories.title: Visual presentation and responsive behavior
categories.signal_terms: Color, text and graphical contrast, responsive reflow, zoom, spacing, hover
categories.diagnostic_question: Does the UI become illegible or lose content when perception or presentation changes?
categories.common_misclassification: Differentiate minimum text contrast, non-text contrast, AAA contrast and user spacing override.

categories.title: Keyboard operation and focus
categories.signal_terms: Keyboard parity, traps, shortcuts, focus order, visible focus
categories.diagnostic_question: Can users complete the operation with keyboard only and determine where focus is?
categories.common_misclassification: Passing a Tab smoke test does not prove keyboard interaction patterns function.

categories.title: Time, interruptions and physical reactions
categories.signal_terms: Timeouts, session preservation, autoplay, moving content, flashes, animation
categories.diagnostic_question: Is the experience time-sensitive, interruptive, flashing or moving in ways users cannot control?
categories.common_misclassification: Do not assume prefers-reduced-motion replaces flashing checks or timer obligations.

categories.title: Pointer, touch and motion input
categories.signal_terms: Gesture alternatives, cancellation, visible label alignment, target size, motion sensors
categories.diagnostic_question: Is an alternative input route missing or a pointer target difficult to operate?
categories.common_misclassification: WCAG 2.2 AA target size is 24 CSS px with exceptions; 2.1 AAA 2.5.5 uses 44 CSS px. Match the selected version.

categories.title: Navigation, orientation and discoverability
categories.signal_terms: Skip links, page titles, link purpose, multiple ways, headings, location
categories.diagnostic_question: Can users understand location and purpose and find content without excessive navigation?
categories.common_misclassification: Check entire page sets and flows; do not classify focus order as only navigation.

categories.title: Language and predictable interaction
categories.signal_terms: Language metadata, vocabulary, readable text, unexpected context changes, consistent identification
categories.diagnostic_question: Is text or interaction meaning misinterpreted because language or context shifts?
categories.common_misclassification: Unexpected content update is not always an unexpected change of context.

categories.title: Forms, input help and error prevention
categories.signal_terms: Field purposes, instructions, identified errors, correction advice, review and reversal
categories.diagnostic_question: Can users identify required inputs, repair errors and avoid irreversible submissions?
categories.common_misclassification: Submission safeguards have defined scopes at AA versus AAA.

categories.title: Assistive technology semantics and asynchronous status
categories.signal_terms: Accessible names, roles, values, ARIA states and live status messages
categories.diagnostic_question: Does an assistive technology user lack programmatically available UI state or status?
categories.common_misclassification: Do not classify ordinary HTML validation defects as failures of WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.1.
